items.title: Portfolio coverage of the physical-risk assessment
items.framework: Project addition; closest: IFRS S2 29(c) / HKEX C2 31; IFRS S2 25(a)(i) / C2 27(a)(i)
items.justification: The asset-level assessment covers 12 assets, 5 of them in Hong Kong (5 of 130 HK assets, about 12% of HK value by our count); portfolio-wide analyses are mentioned but their results are not disclosed.

items.title: Hazards identified and classified, with time horizons
items.framework: TCFD Strategy (a); IFRS S2 10(a)-(d); HKEX C2 20
items.justification: Broad hazard list, defined short / medium / long horizons and physical classification. Note: heat (a chronic physical risk) is presented in the transition-risk table (p. 84).

items.title: Scenario analysis: scenarios used and their range
items.framework: TCFD Strategy (c); IFRS S2 22; HKEX C2 26(b)
items.justification: One physical scenario (SSP5-8.5) for 2030 and 2050; no range of scenarios and none aligned with the latest international agreement.

items.title: Financial quantification of physical risk
items.framework: TCFD Strategy (b), Metrics (a); IFRS S2 15-18; HKEX C2 24-25
items.justification: Current effects are quantified. The portfolio-level anticipated figure is the historical average plus 20%, not scenario-derived; the scenario-based figures cover 12 assets only.

items.title: Methodology transparency (models, data, assumptions, how and when)
items.framework: IFRS S2 22(b); HKEX C2 26(b); TCFD Strategy (c)
items.justification: Provider, date, scenario and asset selection are stated; hazard data, damage and downtime functions, return periods and validation are not.

items.title: Asset-level detail
items.framework: IFRS S2 13(b); HKEX C2 21; TCFD Metrics (a)
items.justification: Per-asset quantified results for 12 assets only; the hazard heat map is colour-only.

items.title: Risk-management process and integration
items.framework: TCFD Risk management (a)-(c); IFRS S2 24-26; HKEX C2 27
items.justification: Identification and integration are stated; how climate risks are assessed for likelihood and magnitude, and prioritised against other risks, is not described.

items.title: Adaptation plans, resourcing and progress
items.framework: TCFD Strategy (b); IFRS S2 14, 29(e); HKEX C2 22, 33
items.justification: Measures, spending and progress are disclosed, with an asset example (Wan Tsui Shopping Centre: climate-related claims down from HK$2.8 million in 2023/24 to zero in 2025/26 after drainage and car park works).

items.title: Physical-risk metrics and targets
items.framework: TCFD Metrics and targets (a)-(c); IFRS S2 29, 33-37; HKEX C2 31, 37-40
items.justification: Claims-based metrics and an exposure-adjusted metric in development; physical-risk targets are qualitative only.

items.title: Governance of climate-related risk
items.framework: TCFD Governance (a)-(b); IFRS S2 5-7; HKEX C2 19
items.justification: Responsible bodies, meeting frequency and management role are disclosed.

items.title: Consistency with observed events
items.framework: Project addition; closest: IFRS S2 15(a) / 16(a); HKEX C2 24(a)
items.justification: Link's disclosed assessment (AXA, 2023/24, compendium p. 78) places Temple Mall North in its lowest damage tier; local media reported its ground floor submerged in September 2023. The assessment accounts for adaptation measures as of 2023/24, which we could not verify. The same assessment states that only surface-water flooding materially affects the assessed assets; Chai Wan Car Service Centre was not among them. At the sea level recorded at Quarry Bay during Typhoon Mangkhut (2018), our model puts the water 0.15 m above the site's entry level and 0.07 m below its lowest floor, so it models no loss.
